t:
Section 4 (33 U.S.C. 1903) is amended—
    (1) by redesignating subsections (b) and (c) as subsections (c) and (d), respectively, and inserting after subsection (a) the following:“(b) Duty of the Administrator.—In addition to other duties specified in this Act, the Administrator and the Secretary, respectively, shall have the following duties and authorities:“(1) The Administrator shall, and no other person may, issue Engine International Air Pollution Prevention certificates in accordance with Annex VI and the International Maritime Organization’s Technical Code on Control of Emissions of Nitrogen Oxides from Marine Diesel Engines, on behalf of the United States for a vessel of the United States as that term is defined in section 116 of title 46, United States Code. The issuance of Engine International Air Pollution Prevention certificates shall be consistent with any applicable requirements of the Clean Air Act or regulations prescribed under that Act.“(2) The Administrator shall have authority to administer regulations 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, and 19 of Annex VI to the Convention.“(3) The Administrator shall, only as specified in section 8(f), have authority to enforce Annex VI of the Convention.”; 
    (2) in subsection (c), as redesignated, by redesignating paragraph (2) as paragraph (4), and inserting after paragraph (1) the following:“(2) In addition to the authority the Secretary has to prescribe regulations under this Act, the Administrator shall also prescribe any necessary or desired regulations to carry out the provisions of regulations 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, and 19 of Annex VI to the Convention.“(3) In prescribing any regulations under this section, the Secretary and the Administrator shall consult with each other, and 
with respect to regulation 19, with the Secretary of the Interior.”; and 
    (3) by adding at the end of subsection (c), as redesignated, the following:“(5) No standard issued by any person or Federal authority, with respect to emissions from tank vessels subject to regulation 15 of Annex VI to the Convention, shall be effective until 6 months after the required notification to the International Maritime Organization by the Secretary.”.

fable.w: The section directs the Administrator to prescribe regulations, and under the definition a grant or mandate of rulemaking authority counts as participation because rulemaking brings in public comment. The tempting reading is to answer No because the only express consultation is between the Secretary, the Administrator and the Secretary of the Interior, which is purely intra-federal. That consultation clause indeed does not count, but the rulemaking mandate independently supports Yes.
fable.s: the Administrator shall also prescribe any necessary or desired regulations to carry out the provisions of regulations 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, and 19 of Annex VI to the Convention.

qwen_block.w: The section requires consultation between federal officials (the Secretary, the Administrator, and the Secretary of the Interior). According to the definition, consultation or coordination between federal agencies or federal officials is intra-government coordination and does not constitute participation. There is no mention of consulting with states, tribes, the public, or other outside entities.
qwen_block.s: In prescribing any regulations under this section, the Secretary and the Administrator shall consult with each other, and with respect to regulation 19, with the Secretary of the Interior.

opus.w: The section requires the Administrator to prescribe regulations. The definition treats required rulemaking as participation, since it opens the decision to public comment. The consultation clause in the same section would not count on its own: it is between the Secretary, the Administrator and the Secretary of the Interior, all federal officials, so it is intra-government coordination. The rulemaking requirement is what makes this a Yes.
opus.s: the Administrator shall also prescribe any necessary or desired regulations to carry out the provisions of regulations 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, and 19 of Annex VI to the Convention.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** The consultation clause ("the Secretary and the Administrator shall consult with each other, and with respect to regulation 19, with the Secretary of the Interior") looks like participation. It isn't, because every party there is a federal official. The same goes for the IMO notification, which is only a notice and gives no outsider a role in the decision. What decides the label is that the section requires the Administrator to prescribe regulations. Under the definition and Example 6, requiring rulemaking counts as participation, because rulemaking brings in public notice and comment.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Administrator and the Secretary to consult with each other, and with the Secretary of the Interior. All these actors (Administrator, Secretary of Homeland Security, Secretary of the Interior) are federal officials inside the federal government. The definition explicitly excludes intra-government coordination as participation. There is no mention of consulting with states, tribes, the public, or other outside entities.
qwen_chat.s: (3) In prescribing any regulations under this section, the Secretary and the Administrator shall consult with each other, and with respect to regulation 19, with the Secretary of the Interior.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "consult with each other" implies participation because it involves coordination. However, the definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination BETWEEN federal agencies or federal officials (e.g., "the Secretary of Labor, in consultation with the Secretary of Health and Human Services") is intra-government coordination and is NOT participation. Here, the Administrator (of the Coast Guard, an agency within the Department of Homeland Security) and the Secretary (of Homeland Security) are both inside the federal government. The consultation with the Secretary of the Interior is also between two federal cabinet secretaries. Therefore, no outside party is involved in the decision-making process described in this specific clause.
